messages:
john_cust: Hi — our app suddenly started getting JSON parse errors from Redwood when using structured_output="json". Happened after the 3/15 routing change. Sample response body we get: ```
Model: redwood-fallback-lite-v1
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Body:
{
  "items": [
    {"id": "abc123", "data": "..."}
  ]
}
```
but the client then crashes with a JSON.parse error reading some responses that look like this: ```
"items": [ {"id":"abc123","data":"..."} ]

Note: no outer braces sometimes, or we get a plain-text apology: "Sorry, I can't provide JSON for that."
```
Any idea? This started after the smart-routing change that added cheaper model variants as fallbacks.

maria_support: Thanks for the report, @john_cust. Can you paste a full raw response (including headers) and a request_id? Also which endpoint and SDK version? :eyes: 

john_cust: Request-id: req_20260315_8f7a2e. Endpoint: /v1/generate with body mode="structured_output" schema=mySchemaV2. SDK: js v2.3.1. Full raw attached below (copied): 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Model: redwood-fallback-lite-v1
Date: Tue, 15 Mar 2026 18:04:12 GMT

Sorry, I can't output JSON for that input. Try a shorter prompt.
```
That is the one that fails parsing.

maria_support: Got it. Reproducing locally now. Escalating to eng with logs & request id. @tom_engineer can you take a look? I'll create an incident if this is a regression.

tom_engineer: Looking. Initial guess: smart routing fell back to a low-cost variant that doesn't honor structured_output enforcement. Can you share the routing policy id? Also pasting our quick repro curl we used: ```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-main","mode":"structured_output","schema":"mySchemaV2","prompt":"..."}' 
```
When our test hit the fallback variant we saw Content-Type: text/plain and non-JSON body.

infra-bot: [routing.debug] request=req_20260315_8f7a2e routed-> redwood-fallback-lite-v1 policy=smart-cost-2 reason=capacity_shortage

maria_support: That's consistent with customer's logs. Is fallback set allowed to return non-JSON? I thought structured_output should be enforced server-side.

tom_engineer: It should. Two possible failure modes: 1) fallback model isn't in the "structured_output_compatible" set so runtime didn't enforce schema, or 2) enforcement hooked into the primary model's metadata and wasn't applied after dynamic routing. I'm seeing (from routing config) that the policy's fallback pool contains redwood-fallback-lite-v1 which is labeled legacy-capable but missing the structured_output flag.

sre_oncall: We should not let a model that can't guarantee schema be used for structured_output requests. Temporary mitigation: block routing fallback when request.mode=="structured_output" or require fallback models to advertise structured_output capability. I'll push a short-lived gate in the router.

maria_support: Timeline for that gate? Customer is seeing production errors.

sre_oncall: I can push a rule to the router config now: reject fallback for structured_output and force queueing/backpressure so request either stays on a compatible model or returns 503 rather than invalid body. Rolling patch in 10-15m, will monitor.

tom_engineer: After gate, we should also add a runtime assertion: if mode==structured_output and body isn't valid JSON that matches the schema, return 502 + structured failure envelope instead of passer-through text. That will avoid client-side crashes. I'll open an internal PR and link here.

maria_support: Thanks. John, short-term workaround: can you pin model=redwood-main or disable smart-routing for your API key? That will avoid fallback into the incompatible family. We'll credit you for the impacted requests.

john_cust: Pinning works as a workaround. Not ideal long-term, but will do for now. Appreciate the quick action.

infra-bot: [deploy] router-config v2026-03-15-7 rolled to canary (10% nodes) by @sre_oncall

sre_oncall: Gate deployed to canary. I'm watching logs for any surge of 503s. If we see customer impact, we can roll back.

tom_engineer: PR #3456 opened: runtime: enforce_structured_output_post_routing. Plan: validate model capabilities during routing selection; if chosen model lacks capability, either select alternate compatible variant or return structured 502. Tests include simulated fallback responses with non-JSON bodies. ETA for merge to main: 24h after review.

maria_support: Created internal support ticket SUP-5121 and credited customer for errors between 2026-03-15T18:00 and 2026-03-15T20:30. Notifying account manager for follow-up.

john_cust: Thank you. Can you also post the exact response shape we should expect on future errors so we can handle gracefully on our side?

tom_engineer: Yes — final decision: if the runtime cannot guarantee structured output we'll return: Content-Type: application/json, HTTP 502, body: `{"error":"structured_output_unavailable","message":"requested output schema cannot be guaranteed by selected model"}`. Please handle that instead of attempting to parse model text. We'll add this to the API docs.

maria_support: Closing loop: gate in canary; PR opened; customer patched by pinning model; support ticket & credits issued. I'll follow up once PR is merged and patch deployed. :white_check_mark: 

john_cust: Great, thanks everyone. Will monitor and reopen if needed.
